items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
Costco sells you a hot dog and a drink for a dollar fifty. It's cost that since nineteen eighty-five.
Narrator
Adjust for inflation, and it'd be around four dollars fifty today. So why hasn't it moved?
Narrator
The story goes, the founder told his successor: raise the hot dog, and I'll kill you.
Narrator
Because the hot dog isn't the product. You are.
Narrator
It's a loss leader: a deal so cheap it pulls you into the store.
Narrator
Last year, Costco sold over two hundred and forty-five million of those combos.
Narrator
But to get in, you need a membership.
Narrator
In its latest year, Costco made about five point nine billion dollars from fees alone.
Narrator
That's roughly two-thirds of its whole profit.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the cheap hot dog isn't losing money. It's selling the membership.
Narrator
So when a deal looks too good, ask what it's really selling you.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
